findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: directory_send_licensing_enquiry · Private data: directory_search, directory_send_licensing_enquiry · Public sink: directory_lookup_work, directory_send_licensing_enquiry, directory_similar_from_owner · Destructive: directory_skill_get.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: directory_send_licensing_enquiry · Private data: directory_search, directory_send_licensing_enquiry · Public sink: directory_lookup_work, directory_send_licensing_enquiry, directory_similar_from_owner · Destructive: directory_skill_get

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "directory_search_recordings" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
